title: Electronic phase separation and emergence of a nondimerized insulating phase in VO$_2$ $(110)_{\mathit{R}}$ ultrathin films
authors: S. Inoue, D. Shiga, R. Hayasaka, K. Ozawa, A. F. Santander-Syro, H. Kumigashira
abstract: Using in situ photoemission spectroscopy and x-ray absorption spectroscopy, we investigated the thickness dependence of the electronic structure and V-V dimerization in VO$_2$/TiO$_2$ (110) ultrathin films, in which the one-dimensional V-V chains along the $c_{\mathit{R}}$ axis lie in the film plane. In VO$_2$ $(110)_{\mathit{R}}$ films, the reduction in dimensionality along the surface-normal direction is not expected to impose a geometric constraint on V-V dimerization, unlike in VO$_2$ $(001)_{\mathit{R}}$ films. Nevertheless, the characteristic spectral changes associated with the temperature-driven metal-insulator transition observed in thick films persist down to 1.5 nm, whereas at 1 nm an insulating electronic phase is observed without V-V dimerization. This behavior is highly similar to that reported for VO$_2$ $(001)_{\mathit{R}}$, suggesting that the enhancement of Mott instability resulting from reduced dimensionality is a common and essential driving force for the emergence of the nondimerized insulating phase in VO$_2$ ultrathin films. Meanwhile, unlike in VO$_2$ $(001)_{\mathit{R}}$, the nondimerized insulating phase in VO$_2$ $(110)_{\mathit{R}}$ coexists with the phase exhibiting the temperature-driven metal-insulator transition. Its fraction increases exponentially with decreasing thickness and becomes dominant at 1 nm. The corresponding effective critical thickness is estimated to be 2.2 nm. These results imply that the geometric orientation of the V-V chains dictates the spatial evolution of electronic phase separation via strain-mediated phase competition.
summary: This experimental study investigates how reducing the thickness of $	ext{VO}_2$ films affects its electronic phase transition. Using advanced spectroscopy, the authors found that the system develops a nondimerized insulating phase driven by enhanced Mott instability, even when the crystal structure suggests otherwise. This work highlights that the geometric orientation of the crystal lattice dictates the spatial evolution of electronic phase separation in these strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the thickness dependence of the electronic structure and V-V dimerization in $	ext{VO}_2 (110)_{	ext{R}}$ ultrathin films, particularly how reduced dimensionality affects the Mott-Peierls transition.
main_result: The emergence of a nondimerized insulating (NI) phase is driven by the enhancement of Mott instability due to reduced dimensionality, and this phase-separation behavior is dictated by the geometric orientation of the V-V chains.
method: The research employed in situ photoemission spectroscopy (PES) and x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) to probe electronic structure and V-V dimerization across varying film thicknesses.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{VO}_2$ (Vanadium dioxide) grown as epitaxial ultrathin films on $	ext{TiO}_2 (110)$ substrates. The material is a strongly correlated oxide known for its temperature-driven metal-insulator transition.
key_observables: Electronic structure (PES/XAS), V-V dimerization (O K-edge XAS), electrical resistivity ($ho$) vs. Temperature ($T$), and the fraction of the nondimerized insulating (NI) phase.
important_parameters: Film thickness ($t$), temperature ($T$), and the critical thickness ($t_c = 2.2 	ext{ nm}$) marking the transition to the NI phase.
main_assumptions: The study assumes that the $	ext{VO}_2 (110)_{	ext{R}}$ orientation minimizes direct geometric constraints on V-V dimerization, allowing the investigation of intrinsic Mott instability effects.
figures_summary: Figures show the temperature dependence of transport properties ($ho(T)$) and spectroscopic data (PES/XAS) revealing the persistence of MIT spectral changes down to 1.5 nm, and the appearance of the NI phase at 1 nm.
paper_structure: The paper systematically measures the electronic structure and dimerization as a function of film thickness, comparing the results to known behavior in other orientations ($	ext{VO}_2 (001)_{	ext{R}}$) to deduce the underlying physical mechanism driving the phase transition.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses how dimensionality and strain mediate phase transitions in correlated oxides, providing experimental evidence for Mott instability enhancement in confined geometries, which is relevant to designing novel correlated quantum materials.
